solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Make plain knitwear for sportsperson (4,6)

blocks.note: to show something is to make it plain
a jumper is a knitted pullover

annotation.surface: Someone decides to wear a simple sweater for a sporting occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make plain' reads as describing the knitwear, but it is a verb meaning SHOW; a show jumper rides horses over fences.
annotation.definitionFit: A show jumper competes in the equestrian sport of jumping fences, so is a sportsperson.

entries.clue: Appeal for help over fair (2-2)

blocks.note: O = over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: A plea for assistance with a fair or funfair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a funfair, but it is the adjective: middling, neither good nor bad.
annotation.definitionFit: So-so means only fair, passable.

entries.clue: Very good variety of grape, tons having been harvested (4)

indicatorNotes.having been harvested: the tons are gathered in and taken away, so T leaves

blocks.note: Tokay is a Hungarian grape and wine

annotation.surface: A fine grape variety whose tons of fruit have been picked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very good' is the reply of assent, as in 'Very good, sir', which is what OKAY means here.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Very good!' as an acknowledgement means the same as 'Okay!'.

entries.clue: Bird in Mississippi city is a byword for speed (4,8)

indicatorNotes.in: the bird goes inside the city

blocks.note: Jackson is the capital of Mississippi

annotation.surface: A bird living in a Mississippi city is famous for being fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before you can say Jack Robinson' is an old British phrase for 'very quickly', hence the byword.
annotation.definitionFit: The name Jack Robinson survives only in the saying for doing something instantly.

entries.clue: Chap importing company wine (5)

indicatorNotes.importing: the chap takes the company inside him

annotation.surface: A man who brings in wine for his firm.
annotation.walkthrough: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine, named after its town.
annotation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a French wine from southern Burgundy.

entries.clue: Thus topless youths around university moon (9)

indicatorNotes.around: the youths go around the university

annotation.surface: Shirtless young men gather around a college, gazing at the moon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thus' is HENCE rather than SO; the topless youths make a fine image, but it is the word 'Thus' that loses its top.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this icy satellite of Saturn, spraying geysers from its south pole, is one of many moons.

entries.clue: Round enclosure unobstructed by buildings (4)

blocks.note: a pen is an animal enclosure

annotation.surface: A circular pen standing in open country with no buildings around it.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition describes open land, free of built-up areas.
annotation.definitionFit: Open country is land not obstructed by buildings.

entries.clue: Pasta course outside during extremely long walk (7,3)

indicatorNotes.outside: the pasta goes outside the word for 'during'

blocks.note: a course or route is a way

annotation.surface: A pasta course eaten partway through a very long hike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pasta course' looks like one item on a menu, but the two words split. The Pennine Way is a 268-mile trail along the Pennine hills in northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: At about 268 miles the Pennine Way is a very long walking trail.

entries.clue: What forgetful wizard may have in that case occasionally? (3,3,4)

blocks.note: a wizard who forgot his wand has NO WAND

annotation.surface: A riddle about what an absent-minded wizard might be carrying.
annotation.walkthrough: The first chunk is read as NO WAND and re-spaced as NOW AND.
annotation.definitionFit: Now and then means from time to time, occasionally.

entries.clue: Inappropriately insert piece of cloth cape in footwear (10)

indicatorNotes.in: patch and cape go inside the sock

blocks.note: a patch is a piece of cloth

annotation.surface: Someone clumsily sewing a patch of cape material into a shoe.
annotation.walkthrough: Spatchcock is best known for splitting a chicken, but it also means to insert a passage where it does not belong.
annotation.definitionFit: A less familiar sense: beyond splitting a bird for grilling, the verb covers wedging an out-of-place remark into a text.

entries.clue: Recognise king instantly (4)

annotation.surface: Spotting a monarch at once.
annotation.walkthrough: To know someone by sight is to recognise them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'I'd know that face anywhere' means you would recognise it.

entries.clue: Monarch put out about closed royal property (7,5)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters of MONARCH PUT are put out of order
indicatorNotes.about: the jumbled letters go around TO

blocks.note: a door pulled to is closed

annotation.surface: A king is thrown out of a royal palace that has been shut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like one phrase, but 'put' is fodder and 'out' the instruction. Hampton Court is Henry VIII's palace on the Thames near London.
annotation.definitionFit: Hampton Court Palace is a royal palace, property of the Crown.

entries.clue: Helen’s involved in setting up defence for Troy’s walls? (12)

indicatorNotes.involved in: Nell is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: setting something up is its creation
Nell is a pet form of Helen; the 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: Helen of Troy is caught up in building the city's defences.
annotation.walkthrough: Helen points to Troy, but she only supplies her nickname NELL. The question mark flags that Troy's walls are a fanciful example of battlements.
annotation.definitionFit: Crenellations are the notched battlements on a defensive wall, such as a city's.

entries.clue: Roughness of Courage’s first taste of bitter? (10)

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of Courage

annotation.surface: Asking how rough a pint of Courage's bitter tastes.
annotation.walkthrough: Courage is a British brewery, so the surface reads as a beer review; bitter is a hoppy British beer, and its flavour is HOPPINESS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used chiefly of water: a sea whipped into short broken waves has that quality.

entries.clue: For highest notes mezzo’s beginning what’s in her inmost body (10)

indicatorNotes.beginning: take the first letter of mezzo

blocks.note: TOP LAS: la is a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A mezzo-soprano's high notes seem to come from deep within her body.
annotation.walkthrough: The singing surface points at the diaphragm, but the inmost body is the cell, whose living contents are protoplasm.
annotation.definitionFit: Protoplasm is the living material inside every cell, the innermost stuff of a body.

entries.clue: Council chasing firm for building material (9)

indicatorNotes.chasing: the council comes after the firm

blocks.note: a board is a governing council

annotation.surface: A council pursuing a company over supplies for construction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective HARD.
annotation.definitionFit: Hardboard is compressed fibre sheet used in building.

entries.clue: Designated area with parking arranged in depot (9)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters of IN DEPOT are rearranged

annotation.surface: A marked-out parking zone laid out in a depot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Designated area' looks like the definition, but 'area' is the letter A and only 'Designated' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Appointed means designated, as in an appointed time or place.

entries.clue: Gather material in place to put away (5)

blocks.note: PL = place, as in street names
to put away food is to eat it

annotation.surface: Collecting fabric into a spot where it can be stored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests tidying up, but it is the slang for eating heartily.
annotation.definitionFit: A dressmaking verb: folding fabric into doubled creases draws it together, so the verb means gathering material.

entries.clue: Trump’s regularly lying about popular leader (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take every other letter of Trump's
indicatorNotes.lying about: the letters lie turned about, back to front

blocks.note: T, U, P: every other letter of TRUMPS

annotation.surface: A jibe that Trump habitually lies about a well-liked leader.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as political gossip, and 'leader' seems to point back at Trump himself, but the leader is a different president.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Vladimir, Russia's president since 2000 bar a spell as prime minister, heads a nation.

entries.clue: Rustic entertainment’s divine beer (9)

annotation.surface: A country show praised for its heavenly beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective praising the beer, but it is a noun: a member of the clergy.
annotation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a musical or dramatic piece on a rural theme.

entries.clue: Profligacy with one million capital in America (12)

blocks.note: Providence is the capital of Rhode Island

annotation.surface: Reckless spending of a million dollars in a US state capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts toward money, but it is a state capital.
annotation.definitionFit: Improvidence, failing to provide for the future, is wasteful profligacy.

entries.clue: Always in literature that is strangely frightening (5)

blocks.note: e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

annotation.surface: Books that are always oddly scary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In literature' marks a poetic word: E'ER for 'ever'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word describes fear with an uncanny, unexplained edge, as in a silent house at night.

entries.clue: Statuette missing head — evidence of earlier damage (4)

indicatorNotes.missing head: the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the Academy Award statuette, minus its O

annotation.surface: A statue with its head knocked off bears the marks of past damage.
annotation.walkthrough: The broken statue makes a vivid picture, but the statuette is the film award.
annotation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left by an old wound.

entries.clue: Primarily stimulate, prod and urge, right? (4)

annotation.definition: Primarily stimulate, prod and urge, right?

indicatorNotes.Primarily: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of Stimulate, Prod, Urge, Right

annotation.surface: A question checking that spurring someone means stimulating and urging them.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: to spur is exactly to stimulate, prod and urge.
annotation.definitionFit: To spur is to urge on, as with the spike on a rider's heel.

entries.clue: A sample of Dixieland’s energy and spirit (4)

indicatorNotes.A sample of: a sample is a small part taken from within

annotation.surface: A taste of Dixieland jazz shows its energy and spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: Dixieland is an early style of jazz, which fits the lively surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Élan is vigorous spirit and flair.

entries.clue: Drink for person leaving prison leading game policeman to London? (7,3)

indicatorNotes.leading: prison comes in front of the rest

blocks.note: in Britain one goes up to London

annotation.surface: A farewell drink for a freed prisoner as a policeman escorts him to London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Person leaving prison' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'leaving'. A stirrup cup was offered to a rider already in the saddle, about to depart.
annotation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a parting drink given to someone about to ride away.

entries.clue: Wrestling ring faced with problem (4)

indicatorNotes.faced with: the problem stands in front of the ring

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

annotation.surface: A wrestling ring confronted by some difficulty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrestling ring' reads as one thing, but 'ring' is the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Japanese style, where heavyweights try to push each other out of a ring, is one kind of wrestling.

entries.clue: Dave Turner turned out the same as Indiana Jones? (10)

indicatorNotes.turned out: the letters are turned out of their order

annotation.surface: Asking whether some Dave Turner grew up to be like Indiana Jones.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: Indiana Jones is the film archaeologist-adventurer.
annotation.definitionFit: The whip-carrying film archaeologist who hunts relics across the globe is the model of a daring thrill-seeker.
